‘NO DOCUMENTS RELATED TO FLOOD CONTROL WERE IN THE BRS BUILDING’

The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) assured the public that no documents related to the ongoing investigation into the flood control anomalies were in the Bureau of Research and Standards (BRS) building that caught fire in Quezon City on Wednesday.

“Initial findings indicate that the fire originated from a computer unit inside the Materials Testing Division that reportedly exploded,” they wrote in a statement.

They also reported that no employees were hurt in the incident, and an investigation team is currently assessing the full extent of the damage.

🚀 BrahMos Missile – India’s Supersonic Powerhouse

Key Facts & Features:

1.Supersonic Speed & Power:
🔹Travels at Mach 2.8–3.5 (3 times the speed of sound).
🔹32× more destructive than the American Tomahawk missile.
🔹Combines kinetic energy and a warhead to destroy hardened targets.

https://t.co/kyP7UXXyr5 & Development:
🔹Conceptualised after the Gulf War, India sought advanced missile technology.
🔹1998: BrahMos Aerospace formed as a joint venture between DRDO (India) & NPO Mashinostroyenia (Russia).
🔹Name comes from Brahmaputra + Moskva rivers.
🔹First launch: June 12, 2001, Chandipur, Odisha.

3.Advanced Propulsion:
🔹Two-stage system: solid-propellant booster + liquid-fueled ramjet.
🔹Air-breathing ramjet allows sustained supersonic flight and fuel efficiency.

4.Guidance & Precision:
🔹Uses fire-and-forget technology.
🔹Multi-layer navigation: GPS, GLONASS, NavIC, GAGAN.
🔹Indian-developed G3OM chip ensures targeting accuracy within 5 meters.

5.Stealth & Maneuverability:
🔹Extremely low radar cross-section.
🔹Can perform sea-skimming attacks (5 m) and high-altitude maneuvers (up to 15 km).
🔹Executes high-G “S” maneuvers and steep terminal dives, making interception nearly impossible.

6.Universal Launch Capability:
🔹Land: Mobile Autonomous Launchers (Army use since 2007).
🔹Sea: Warships with vertical and inclined launchers; BrahMos-LR with 800 km range.
🔹Air: Integrated with Sukhoi-30MKI fighter jets; air-launched version carries larger warheads.
🔹Submarine: BrahMos-NG to be deployed on P75I class submarines.

7.Combat Proven:
🔹May 2025 – Operation Sindoor: Struck multiple Pakistani military targets.
🔹Unstoppable: Enemy air defense systems, including HQ-9B, failed to intercept.

8.Next-Gen BrahMos:
🔹BrahMos NG: 50% lighter, smaller, more stealthy, same Mach 3.5 speed.
🔹BrahMos-II: Hypersonic variant planned with Mach 7–8 speeds.

9.Indigenization & Production:
🔹Initially 65% components supplied by Russia; India increased indigenous content to 85%.
🔹New Lucknow facility producing 100–150 missiles annually.
🔹Supported by over 200 Indian companies.

10.Export & Global Recognition:
🔹Philippines: First export customer (375 million USD order).
🔹Interest from Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Middle East & South America.

💡 Summary:

data.cleaned_text: 🚀 BrahMos Missile – India’s Supersonic Powerhouse Key Facts & Features: 1.Supersonic Speed & Power: 🔹Travels at Mach 2.8–3.5 (3 times the speed of sound). 🔹32× more destructive than the American Tomahawk missile. 🔹Combines kinetic energy and a warhead to destroy hardened targets. & Development: 🔹Conceptualised after the Gulf War, India sought advanced missile technology. 🔹1998: BrahMos Aerospace formed as a joint venture between DRDO (India) & NPO Mashinostroyenia (Russia). 🔹Name comes from Brahmaputra + Moskva rivers. 🔹First launch: June 12, 2001, Chandipur, Odisha. 3.Advanced Propulsion: 🔹Two-stage system: solid-propellant booster + liquid-fueled ramjet. 🔹Air-breathing ramjet allows sustained supersonic flight and fuel efficiency. 4.Guidance & Precision: 🔹Uses fire-and-forget technology. 🔹Multi-layer navigation: GPS, GLONASS, NavIC, GAGAN. 🔹Indian-developed G3OM chip ensures targeting accuracy within 5 meters. 5.Stealth & Maneuverability: 🔹Extremely low radar cross-section. 🔹Can perform sea-skimming attacks (5 m) and high-altitude maneuvers (up to 15 km). 🔹Executes high-G “S” maneuvers and steep terminal dives, making interception nearly impossible. 6.Universal Launch Capability: 🔹Land: Mobile Autonomous Launchers (Army use since 2007). 🔹Sea: Warships with vertical and inclined launchers; BrahMos-LR with 800 km range. 🔹Air: Integrated with Sukhoi-30MKI fighter jets; air-launched version carries larger warheads. 🔹Submarine: BrahMos-NG to be deployed on P75I class submarines. 7.Combat Proven: 🔹May 2025 – Operation Sindoor: Struck multiple Pakistani military targets. 🔹Unstoppable: Enemy air defense systems, including HQ-9B, failed to intercept. 8.Next-Gen BrahMos: 🔹BrahMos NG: 50% lighter, smaller, more stealthy, same Mach 3.5 speed. 🔹BrahMos-II: Hypersonic variant planned with Mach 7–8 speeds. 9.Indigenization & Production: 🔹Initially 65% components supplied by Russia; India increased indigenous content to 85%. 🔹New Lucknow facility producing 100–150 missiles annually. 🔹Supported by over 200 Indian companies. 10.Export & Global Recognition: 🔹Philippines: First export customer (375 million USD order). 🔹Interest from Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Middle East & South America. 💡 Summary: From a collaborative Russian engine project to India’s most feared supersonic missile, BrahMos combines speed, precision, stealth, and universal deployment. It has redefined India’s defense capabilities and proven itself in real combat scenarios, establishing India as a global leader in advanced missile technology. #OperationSindoor
